# Findings: from generated references to editable pixel art

## 1. The actual objective

**User requirement:** retain the original character's aesthetic, vibe, expressions and recognizable identity, with small differences and grid-appropriate simplification. Additional references may be generated by the agent or supplied by the user. Exact raster reproduction is not the acceptance test.

**Proposed approach:** combine a canonical style/identity reference set, targeted supplemental generation, deterministic image preparation and native pixel finishing. Compare methods on small assets before choosing a production route. This is a research-backed hypothesis to test, not a proven automatic pipeline.

## 2. What existing craft supports

Aseprite's reference layers can display an image at a higher resolution than the drawing canvas. They are guides rather than editable paint layers. Its layer/command APIs also support organization and transferring selected pixels; the installed tool interface must still be tested for the operations required. [S01–S03](SOURCES.md)

Medeiros documents a workflow in which rough rendered reference is reduced in size/palette, then redrawn on another layer and given revised timing. This is a useful precedent for reference-assisted work; it does not establish that our agent can perform it with high likeness. [S04](SOURCES.md)

Pixel art requires purposeful clusters, contours, shading and feature choices. Neither a tiny image nor a limited palette alone establishes that craftsmanship. Hand-placed transition colors and meaningful single-pixel marks can be legitimate, so indiscriminate smoothing bans or speckle removal can damage faces. [S06](SOURCES.md)

**Implication for this project:** choose the construction method by appearance and editability, not by whether every source pixel was independently invented. A traced/conversion-derived asset can be useful; a mechanically valid independent redraw can still miss the desired face.

## 3. Why multiple references are useful

The user is not restricted to one photograph-like source. A generated clean full-body view can make silhouettes easier to isolate; a close-up can clarify an expression; an alternate pose/view can propose hidden surfaces; a strip can propose action phases. Each solves a different task. This expansion is authorized by the user's request, not evidence that generated outputs will be mutually consistent.

OpenAI documents image/edit workflows and cautions that recurring-character consistency and precise composition can still fail. Its image tool accepts reference-image inputs. ChatGPT's editor may change regions beyond a selection. These capabilities justify obtaining additional candidates, while the limitations justify checking each before native production. [S11–S13](SOURCES.md)

Gemini's developer documentation likewise covers text/image generation and editing, with model-dependent controls. We have not authenticated this user's account or mapped its web controls to an API. [S14](SOURCES.md)

**Proposed control:** keep canonical identity/style images attached to every relevant request. Add an accepted native sprite and the needed pose brief where appropriate. Do not recursively replace the original identity with successive generated variants. Permit legitimate changes of expression for the requested action, rather than forcing a resting smile onto an attack frame.

## 4. Geometry transfer and source-derived seeds

Tracing guides preserve selected boundaries; color sampling reduces guessing about material relationships; masks identify regions for separate handling. Direct reduction preserves the sampled geometry but may lose a thin eyelid or mouth. None of these steps automatically provides the underlying semantic parts, hidden surfaces, animation timing or clean pixel clusters.

Three reasonable experimental routes are:

| Route | Expected benefit, to test | Main failure risk |
|---|---|---|
| Trace-guided native drawing | Keep silhouette and landmark placement while authoring readable clusters | Agent still interprets interior forms incorrectly |
| Conversion plus cleanup | Preserve more original geometry/color and reduce reconstruction work | Aliasing, merged features, noisy shading or weak native separation |
| Hybrid | Keep stable source-derived shapes while redrawing only weak areas; obtain better references when helpful | Too many uncontrolled changes obscure what improved |

These benefits are hypotheses, not measured speedups. Compare routes before adding more tools.

## 5. Downscaling and the native grid

Pillow distinguishes nearest-neighbor selection, area averaging and higher-order filtering. They preserve different aspects of the source; “nearest neighbor everywhere” is not a general solution for illustration reduction. The kit uses nearest-neighbor enlargement for finished-grid inspection, and explicit reduction choices for seeds. [S07](SOURCES.md)

There is a mathematical limit: fewer output samples cannot preserve every independently varying source detail. This does not imply that identity or aesthetic must be lost; the task is to preserve the important information and redesign lesser features deliberately. A correct output file size also says nothing about whether apparent pixels inside a generated image sit on a consistent logical grid.

**Local historical evidence:** the fixed 420×315 crop was reduced to 56×42, 84×63 and 112×84 using a shared illustrative 32-color palette. The supplied comparisons show recognizable broad geometry, with reduced clarity in small eyelids/mouth details at the lower grid. These are crop seeds with a background, not transparent native assets, approved resolutions or measured likeness scores. See `examples/previous_conversion/` for method and prior checks.

The new helper exposes exact crop, size, reduction filter, optional palette and alpha policy. Its explicit parameters make processing reproducible; they do not choose a good art direction.

## 6. Optional techniques, not mandatory installs

**PixelOE:** its implementation uses contrast-aware outline expansion in pixelization. It may help preserve small dark boundaries, but changed edge thickness may alter an expression. It is a worthwhile optional test if simple reductions fail a named feature; no result on this character is claimed. [S08](SOURCES.md)

**Segmentation:** SAM 2 provides segmentation masks. Such masks could assist extraction or visible-part selection, but a mask does not infer the hidden jacket behind an arm or produce an animation rig. Use existing masks/simple selections first if adequate. [S09](SOURCES.md)

**Structure-conditioned generation:** ControlNet's paper describes controls based on edges, depth, segmentation and pose. This may help construct a supplementary pose reference; it is still generation, not guaranteed exact copying. No new diffusion stack is needed merely because this technique exists. [S10](SOURCES.md)

**Other representations:** a rough 3D pose reference or cutout rig can help with many rotations or reusable parts. They require their own evidence and setup. Keep them as alternatives when a measured bottleneck warrants a test, not an automatic replacement for the Aseprite goal.

## 7. Style and image-generation requests

Requests should name the attached source as the same original character and specify which change is allowed. Describe material colors, hair structure, proportions, selective contours, shading planes and the desired expression instead of relying only on a game's name. The user asks for a near-lookalike, not a generic character sharing an outfit.

Ask for lower detail by simplifying secondary strands/folds/texture while keeping identity-bearing shapes. “Less detailed” alone may produce a different genre or chibi design. Prompt settings are proposals; inspect the result. Do not force an arbitrary total of 16/32 colors unless the experiment specifically calls for it.

Separate cinematic mood from asset clarity. A neutralized reference may help extraction but must retain the material relationships and line/shading character that the user likes. Test the finished asset against an appropriate scene before deciding that the atmosphere survived. Consistency may be managed separately for world art and portraits, but deliberate internal consistency remains important. [S05](SOURCES.md)

## 8. Animation needs coherence, not one-image derivation

A coherent sheet and individually generated poses are both permitted. A sheet may improve shared context, while individual frames can provide more room for corrections. Neither guarantees anatomy, timing, layout or identity. Prefer the smaller experiment that tests the required action and review every frame.

Normalize crops, scale, anchors and palette as a set. Do not independently stretch each pose to its bounding box: that changes body scale as limbs extend. Do not align every pose's lowest visible pixel to the same ground line: that can erase jumps. Preserve intentional root movement in explicit offsets or the engine track. These are this kit's engineering/design rules, not proof of a successful animation.

Aseprite supports timeline, cel and per-frame-duration workflows; Godot can play individual frames or a sprite sheet. Those are documented integration mechanisms. Actual fluidity, contact, identity and gameplay readability require played review, not only a contact sheet. [S15–S16](SOURCES.md)

## 9. Current evidence and next decision

Repository records show genuine layered construction and increasingly strict review/checks, but the latest head study still has unapproved likeness gaps. The earlier failed resolution studies changed geometry/framing, so they did not isolate resolution as the cause. See [workspace evidence](WORKSPACE_EVIDENCE.md).

**Recommended next decision:** test whether reference-guided tracing or conversion-plus-cleanup better retains this identity at one comparable native layout. Get a simpler/missing-angle reference only for a named gap. If both fail, diagnose the failure class—source, mapping, detail budget, drawing quality, style mismatch or tool access—before increasing the grid or generating a whole new scene.

The acceptance target is a convincing, revisable game-oriented asset in the approved visual style. The strict technical equality target applies only to immutable originals, locked parts and reproducible operations, not the entire new drawing.
